S037-01.notes: 'so far outside that range' + suspected faulty instrument = anomalous. routine contradicts; conclusive contradicts the recheck; redundant illogical.

S037-02.notes: Dish rack, parking meter, puddle = everyday/mundane. Others don't fit the examples.

flags: minor: Andes detail (torpor more frequent/deeper with low fat reserves) is a simplification of Wolf et al. 2020, which linked torpor use to lower body mass/energy state; acceptable but could be softened
S037-03.notes: Text explains torpor as survival strategy for cold nights given high metabolism. A, C, D unsupported/too narrow.

flags: minor: key is the longest choice and the only compound statement; distractors are weakly attractive (A directly contradicted by cross-fostering, C by 'more varied' chirps)
S037-04.notes: Cross-fostered pups adopt foster dialect -> learned; queen removal destabilizes dialect -> queen helps maintain it. Consistent with Barker et al. 2021 (Science).

S037-05.notes: Conclusion requires comparison of observer vs. no-observer rates; only A gives both. B and C give single values; D obscures the difference. No distractor supports the full claim.

S037-06.notes: Mirrors Vander Wall's landmark-shift experiment (1982): probes displaced with landmarks implicates landmark memory specifically. B supports memory over random search but does not isolate landmarks (could be smell of own caches?); A and D irrelevant.

S037-07.notes: Quarry tools, platforms, hearths, and stone-shaped gaps at Preseli outcrops (Craig Rhos-y-felin, Carn Goedog) indicate human quarrying, countering glacial transport. A contradicts text; C contradicts the Welsh source; D unsupported. ~230 km distance is accurate.

S037-08.notes: Only C names the source of the clue (1,600-year-old text, Ge Hong). Facts (1969 start, >2,000 remedies, low-temperature extraction, 2015 Nobel shared) accurate.

S037-09.notes: Drawbacks then continued standard status = contrast/concession: Still. ~50,000-year limit accurate.

S037-10.notes: Past perfect 'had written'. wrote is nonstandard past participle; writing/writes ungrammatical after had.
